scope: First Bay Area flagship editorial tranche. Not published.
principles: Representative buildings are presentation examples only.
District intelligence comes from the broader raw corpus, assignment review, diversity review, spatial patterns, and editorial review.
Public copy should be restrained, spatial, comparison-oriented, and free of source/provenance/confidence language.

raw_corpus_review.assignment_quality: Strong high-confidence assignment set with limited medium-confidence drift.
raw_corpus_review.diversity_note: Large building/contact breadth, but original company/provenance coverage is thin and LMS dominates the listing layer. Keep source caveats internal.

positioning.headline: East Bay institutional business core with BART access, civic adjacency, and professional office depth.
positioning.summary: Downtown Oakland is the formal business core of the East Bay, centered on Broadway, City Center, civic institutions, BART access, and older downtown office buildings.
best_fit: Legal, nonprofit, civic-adjacent, and professional service teams
Organizations that need regional transit access
Companies comparing East Bay value with San Francisco CBD presence
positioning.access_pattern: BART-first downtown access with regional East Bay and San Francisco comparison value.

editorial_interpretation_input.heading: How to read Downtown Oakland
editorial_interpretation_input.opening_statement: Downtown Oakland is the East Bay's formal business core: civic institutions, BART access, professional office buildings, and older downtown blocks clustered around Broadway and City Center.
paragraphs: It fits organizations that want regional transit access, public-sector or nonprofit adjacency, and a more practical East Bay alternative to San Francisco's Financial District.
Compared with Uptown, Downtown Oakland reads more institutional and office-oriented. Compared with Jack London Square, it is less waterfront and more civic and transit focused.

nearby_comparisons.public_note: More mixed-use and smaller-company oriented, with stronger Uptown arts and retail context.
More waterfront and warehouse-adjacent, with service-commercial and adaptive texture.
Smaller-scale historic blocks just west of the formal downtown core.
More traditional regional CBD setting across the bay, usually with stronger client-facing downtown presence.

Companies that want more street-level context than a formal CBD

positioning.access_pattern: Transit-oriented East Bay access with a more mixed-use feel than Downtown Oakland.

editorial_interpretation_input.heading: How to read Uptown Oakland
editorial_interpretation_input.opening_statement: Uptown Oakland is the more mixed-use counterpart to Downtown Oakland, with office buildings, arts venues, food, apartments, BART access, and Lake Merritt-adjacent commercial blocks sharing a tighter urban setting.
paragraphs: It works for teams that want East Bay access and professional office options without the formality of the civic downtown core.
Compared with Downtown Oakland, Uptown feels less institutional and more mixed-use. Compared with Jack London Square, it is less waterfront and more Broadway/Lake Merritt oriented.
avoid: positioning it as a second Downtown Oakland
overstating creative/adaptive reuse without representative examples

editorial_interpretation_input.heading: How to read Downtown Palo Alto
editorial_interpretation_input.opening_statement: Downtown Palo Alto is a compact Peninsula business district where low-rise office buildings, restaurants, retail, Caltrain access, and startup/professional-service demand sit close together.
paragraphs: It fits teams that want a walkable client-facing address rather than a campus or highway-corridor office setting.

Compared with Mountain View, Downtown Palo Alto is more premium and downtown-oriented. Compared with Redwood City, it is smaller and more tightly tied to startup, venture, and professional-service routines.
avoid: blurring with Stanford Research Park or California Avenue

editorial_interpretation_input.heading: How to read South San Francisco Biotech Corridor
editorial_interpretation_input.opening_statement: The South San Francisco Biotech Corridor is not a generic office market; it is a lab, R&D, flex, and industrial-support geography shaped by Oyster Point, Gateway, Lindenville, 101 access, and proximity to the airport.
paragraphs: It fits companies that need technical space, campus or business-park settings, and operational access more than a traditional downtown office address.

Compared with Mission Bay, South San Francisco is more freeway and campus-oriented. Compared with Downtown Palo Alto or Redwood City, it is less client-facing and more tied to life science, flex, and industrial support patterns.

positioning.headline: Waterfront Oakland commercial district with office, service-commercial, warehouse-adjacent, and adaptive texture.
positioning.summary: Jack London Square should read as Oakland's waterfront commercial alternative: office and retail near the estuary, older warehouse and service-commercial blocks, ferry/rail/port adjacency, and a different physical feel from Downtown or Uptown.
best_fit: Teams seeking waterfront identity near downtown Oakland
Companies comparing downtown office with adaptive or waterfront context
positioning.access_pattern: Downtown-adjacent waterfront access with ferry, rail, port, and I-880 context.

editorial_interpretation_input.heading: How to read Jack London Square
editorial_interpretation_input.opening_statement: Jack London Square is Oakland's waterfront commercial district, where office and retail sit near warehouse-adjacent blocks, service-commercial streets, ferry access, rail lines, and the port edge.
paragraphs: It fits users that want Oakland access with a less formal, more physical commercial setting than Downtown or Uptown.

Compared with Downtown Oakland, Jack London Square is more waterfront and service-commercial. Compared with Uptown, it is less arts-and-Broadway oriented and more tied to the estuary, warehouse texture, and operational access.
